recipes.name: Tempered White Chocolate Couverture
recipes.competencyFocus: Use cookery methods for centres and fillings to achieve full flavoured, interesting and natural characteristics. Manipulate ingredients at correct temperature to achieve the correct viscosity and consistency.
recipes.evidenceTags: Evidence tags: Base │ Tempering │ White couverture
method: In a microwave safe bowl, heat 3/4 of chocolate for 20 seconds and stir. Repeat this step until most of the chocolate is melted.
Check the temperature. If you are close to (40C) start heating in 5 second intervals, stirring between each cycle and rechecking temperature as it can heat quickly in the end stages and burn.
Add in the remaining chocolate. Continue to stir until the temperature drops to (30C.) Your chocolate is now in temper and ready to use.

Test: Spread a small spoonful of chocolate on a piece of wax paper. If it looks dull or streaky, re-temper the chocolate. If it dries quickly with a glossy finish and no streaks, the chocolate is in temper.

Tip: Once melted chocolate has been tempered, it must be used before it cools and sets. If it cools to 27C and is still fairly liquid, it can be reheated to a liquid consistency. If it has completely cooled and solidified, it should be re-tempered.
To hold: If you keep your chocolate within these temperature ranges, it will stay in temper and be liquid enough to use you can hold it over a warm water bath or in a chocolate temper machine/warmer.
recipes.test: Dip a test strip and set it aside at room temperature. At three to five minutes it should be firm, evenly glossy and free of streaks.
recipes.tip: White couverture scorches before it melts through. Use short microwave bursts with stirring between, and never take it above 45 °C.
storage: Hold tempered couverture at its working temperature in a tempering machine or over a warm water bath
Do not refrigerate
Store solid couverture at 16–18 °C, 50–60% relative humidity, sealed and away from strong odours.
recipes.presentationStandard: Glossy, even, no streaking or bloom; clean snap when set.
recipes.assessorNotes: Build notes — items flagged, not filled (assessor guide): Recipe cards with no yield. Recipes 1 to 3 (the tempered couverture cards, MVC1845 to MVC1847) record no yield and no portion size, so a learner who selects one of them for Theory Question 1 cannot calculate a conversion factor. The worked key redirects the learner to a card that states a yield. The three cards need a yield and portion size added at the next revision.

recipes.name: Rocher, Mendiant - Fruit and Nut
recipes.competencyFocus: Fruit and nut filling, hard centre, hand shaped uniform sizing, tempered chocolate.
recipes.evidenceTags: Evidence tags: Hard centre │ Cut or dressed │ Nuts │ Fruits
method: Almond Rocher
Moisten the almonds with the liqueur.
Dust icing sugar over the almonds.
Spread the almonds onto a sheet pan and roast at 170 °C until golden brown. Allow to cool.
Warm a bowl with a torch or by placing it in the oven for 10 seconds. Warming the bowl first stops the couverture setting too quickly.
Place the almonds in the warm bowl. Add the cocoa butter, then the tempered couverture, and stir to coat the nuts.
Spoon small portions onto parchment paper.
Hold at room temperature for 30 minutes to allow the couverture to set.
Hazelnut Praline
Toast the hazelnuts with the skin on. Allow to cool, keeping some whole and crushing the rest.
Bring the sugar and water to the boil and cook to a light golden toffee.
Add the hazelnuts and pour directly onto parchment paper to stop the cooking. Do this just before the desired colour, as the toffee continues to darken.
Once cool, break up the praline and process in a blender to a medium crumb or paste.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a non-stick mat.
Mix the crushed wafers, hazelnut praline and hazelnut spread together until well combined. The mixture will be sticky.
Refrigerate for about 30 minutes so the mixture firms up.
Shape into teaspoon-sized balls, placing a whole hazelnut inside each one, and freeze for 15 minutes.
Coat in melted couverture and roll in the finely chopped toasted hazelnuts.
Hold at room temperature for 30 minutes to allow the couverture to set.
Store in an airtight container in a cool, dark place.
Note: Alternative styles for the rocher: milk, white or dark couverture; seeds, shaved or desiccated coconut; crushed nuts, skin on or skin off; raw sugar.
Note: the mendiant named in the card title has no method recorded in the source recipe — confirm with your assessor before production.
recipes.test: Break one cooled cluster. The couverture should snap cleanly and the nuts should stay bound rather than falling apart.
recipes.tip: Warm the bowl before you add the nuts. A cold bowl sets the couverture before you have finished coating them.
storage: Store finished pieces at 16–18 °C in a sealed container away from light and odour
Do not refrigerate
Label with production date and use-by.
recipes.presentationStandard: Even cluster size, rough natural surface, nuts and fruit visible, glossy coating.

Roll level tablespoon measures of cream cheese mixture into balls.

method: Place about half of your chocolate into a small pan over a very low heat and heat the chocolate until it reaches a temperature of 45ºC
Decant the melted chocolate into a bowl and add a piece of the un-melted. Stir the chocolate in until it has melted

Keep adding pieces of the un-melted chocolate until the temperature has been reduced to the working temperature for the couverture you are using — see the tempered white, milk and dark couverture recipes
Ensure your mould have been prepared correctly. Pour the melted chocolate into the mould. Fill each of the shapes you’re using to the top.
Once filled, tip the mould upside down over the bowl you stirred the chocolate in and tip out any excess

Put the mould into the fridge for at least half an hour to set

method: Preheat oven to 140°C. Line the base and sides of a baking tray with baking paper.

method: Prepare the raspberry jelly to the workbook recipe. Pour into a frame to a depth of 10 mm. Set for 4 hours at 18–20 °C until firm enough to cut cleanly.

method: Boil the caster sugar and water to 108 °C to form a syrup. Cool the syrup to 30 °C before adding alcohol, so the liqueur does not flash off.
Stir in the orange liqueur and zest. Do not reheat after adding.
Fill each hollow sphere to 3 mm below the opening, leaving space for the seal. Rest for 2 hours at 18 °C so a light sugar crust forms on the surface of the filling.
Temper the dark couverture to a working temperature of 31–32 °C. Seal the base of each sphere and scrape flush with a palette knife.
Set at 16 °C, then pipe filigree decoration with the remaining tempered couverture.
Store at 16–18 °C. Label with a four-week best-before date because of the alcohol content.
Note: syrup batches below 200 g are difficult to boil accurately. Scale up and reserve the balance for the next production run if a larger batch is practical.

recipes.tip: Rest the filled spheres two hours before sealing, so a light sugar crust forms and the seal does not sink into the syrup.

extractionNotes: Source of record for the cards is the learner workbook (SAMPLE_RecipeWorkbook.txt). The assessor guide (SAMPLE_AG_RW.txt) mirrors all fifteen cards word for word and carries NO per-card benchmark, model answer or assessor panel — consistent with the house standard note 'No per-card assessor content'. Where assessorNotes is populated it is taken verbatim from the guide's closing 'Build notes — items flagged, not filled' section, which names specific cards. '||' separates two distinct build notes within one assessorNotes value.

Assessor-guide model answers and worked keys that reference MVC1856, MVC1854 and MVC1850 belong to Theory Question 1, Theory Question 2 and the Case Study, not to the recipe cards, and have deliberately not been attached to those cards (they are in the front-matter agent's scope).

Both source files are flattened single-line text dumps with no line breaks. Header table values, ingredient rows, Test / Tip / Presentation standard lines and storage bullets are unambiguous. METHOD STEP BOUNDARIES WERE INFERRED from sentence structure and the house card anatomy — no wording was added, removed or altered, but the split points between steps are a reconstruction.

Label stripping: the leading labels 'Test: ', 'Tip: ' and 'Presentation standard: ' have been removed from the stored values so a renderer can re-apply them. The 'Evidence tags:' line is stored in full, including its │ (U+2502) separators, as instructed.

Label artefact worth checking against the Word original: cards 1, 2, 3, 6, 7 and 8 show NO literal 'Test:' label before the test sentence in the text dump, whereas cards 4, 5 and 9 to 15 do. The test text itself is present on every card and has been captured.

Cards 1 to 3 carry the source recipe's trailing 'Test:', 'Tip:' and 'To hold:' paragraphs INSIDE the method block, before the card's own Test and Tip lines. These have been kept as method steps 4, 5 and 6 and were not moved into the test/tip fields. These three cards therefore have 6 method steps, outside the house 3-to-5 range.

GARBLED: card 3 (MVC1847) method step 6 is truncated in the source — it ends '...or in a chocolate temper' with no following word. Cards 1 and 2 read '...or in a chocolate temper machine/warmer.' at the same point. Reproduced as found, not completed.

Card 4 (MVC1848) is the only card that groups ingredients: ALMOND ROCHER (5 rows) and HAZELNUT PRALINE (7 rows), captured in the component field. Its method also carries the sub-headings 'Almond Rocher' and 'Hazelnut Praline', retained in position as method entries, plus two trailing 'Note:' paragraphs, also retained as method entries.
